battle.name: 伊孫佐戰役
battle.brief: 一九一五年六月二十三日，義大利在伊松佐河兩岸向奧匈帝國發動第一次攻勢，卡爾索台地與戈里齊亞橋頭堡的拉鋸由此拉開，此後連續十二場戰役打到一九一七年十月。卡面這門一八六〇年的加特林機槍當年已屬舊世代，但它確立的連排機槍射擊與水冷供彈原理，正是前線改用菲亞特・雷維利機槍時所承接的骨幹。

kit.name: 加特林機槍
kit.history: 六根管子用人力轉動。它的後坐力分散在六次上，所以能壓住一個師。

countries: 這場戰爭是義大利王國在第一次世界大戰東南戰線同奧匈帝國的較量，時間由一九一五年六月延伸到一九一七年十月。義軍由陸軍總司令路易吉・卡多納統率，下分第一、第二、第三三個集團軍，戰線自亞得里亞海岸的西斯特米亞納灘頭沿伊松佐河伸向朱利安阿爾卑斯山；下段第三集團軍由阿奧斯塔公爵艾曼努埃萊・菲利貝托指揮，負責壓住戈里齊亞橋頭堡與卡爾索台地，上段第二集團軍由路易吉・迪亞茲掌握，守住上伊松佐與普雷卡伊山口。編制上，義軍步兵師仍以九個營為骨幹，每營約五百人，並混編本土守備師與戰前新編師，另設山地旅、砲兵旅、工程兵、醫療與輜重部隊。奧匈方面，總司令康拉德・馮・赫岑多夫坐鎮維也納兼掌陸軍部，伊松佐正面交由第三集團軍及後設的伊松佐集團軍群統一指揮，司令為塞沃扎爾・博雷維奇，下轄第一、第三、第六集團軍，另有北面的蒂羅爾方面軍集群與東面的多瑙河方面軍集群牽制俄軍。奧軍因此能以少量精銳營抵擋義軍的人數優勢，並把堡壘、臼砲與地形的優勢推到極致。
countriesEn: This war was the duel between the Kingdom of Italy and Austria-Hungary on the south-eastern front of the First World War, running from June 1915 to October 1917. The Italian army was commanded by General Luigi Cadorna and divided into the 1st, 2nd and 3rd Armies, the line running from the beach at Sistemiana on the Adriatic up the Isonzo river towards the Julian Alps; the lower 3rd Army, under the Duke of Aosta, Emanuele Filiberto, was responsible for holding the Gorizia bridgehead and the Carso plateau, while the upper 2nd Army under Luigi Diaz covered the upper Isonzo and the Plevna pass. Structurally an Italian infantry division still rested on nine battalions of about five hundred men each, mixing homeland depot divisions with the newly raised wartime divisions, and there were alpine brigades, artillery brigades, engineer, medical and supply units alongside them. On the Austrian side, Commander-in-Chief Conrad von Hötzendorf sat in Vienna with the War Ministry in the same chair, and the Isonzo front was run by the 3rd Army and later by the Isonzo Army Group under Svetozar Boroević, with the 1st, 3rd and 6th Armies beneath him, while the Tyrol Army Group in the north and the Danube group in the east held back Russia. Austria-Hungary could therefore meet Italian numbers with a small number of picked battalions, and pushed the advantage of fortresses, heavy mortars and terrain to the limit.
people: 關鍵人物分屬兩個指揮系統。義軍最高權力在卡多納手上，他主張以連續攻勢逼迫奧軍消耗，把全軍主力壓在東線，拒絕在阿爾卑斯方向同時大舉出擊；一九一五年六月的第一次攻勢正是在他堅持下發動，而攻勢缺乏充分砲火準備、步兵在無遮蔽坡面成建制傷亡，也正是他戰術性格的第一次亮相。下段第三集團軍由阿奧斯塔公爵率領，他於一九一五年十月在戈里齊亞西岸奪取橋頭堡，一九一六年八月攻入戈里齊亞城，一九一七年十月在卡爾索實施突破，因此被後世稱為「卡爾索之狼」；上段第二集團軍後由路易吉・迪亞茲接手，他在一九一七年十月的卡多里納戰役中把義軍推進到縱深地帶。奧方以康拉德為最高統帥，他以持久消耗對付義軍的速決期望；博雷維奇以嚴防與縱深砲兵逐步穩住前線，頂住了義軍多次正面強攻，卻在卡爾索這種被自己長期改造為堡壘的地形上逐漸失去主動。技術與基層方面，工程兵在岩層下挖出的隧道與地下道路、觀察與校射小組、以及以卡普羅尼雙發轟炸機執行的定點轟炸，都直接決定了攻勢的成敗；一九一七年義軍大量起用未滿十八歲的少年兵補上缺員，使這套以消耗換取推進的作戰方式走到極限。
peopleEn: The decisive figures belong to two separate command systems. Ultimate authority on the Italian side rested with Cadorna, who believed in relentless offensive pressure to grind down the Austro-Hungarian army, concentrated the bulk of the national army on the eastern front and refused a major effort in the Alps at the same time; the first offensive of June 1915 was launched on his insistence, and the short artillery preparation and the loss of whole battalions on open slopes were the first showing of his tactical temperament. The lower 3rd Army was led by the Duke of Aosta, who seized the bridgehead on the Gorizia bank in October 1915, entered the town of Gorizia in August 1916 and broke through on the Carso in October 1917, which is why he was afterwards called the Wolf of the Carso; the upper 2nd Army eventually passed to Luigi Diaz, who drove the Italians into the Austrian rear during the Cadorina offensive of October 1917. On the Austrian side Conrad was the supreme commander, seeking a war of attrition against Italian hopes of a quick decision, while Boroević steadied the front with careful defence and deep artillery, holding off repeated frontal Italian attacks but gradually losing the initiative on ground his own engineers had turned into a fortress. At the technical and rank-and-file level, the tunnels and underground roads driven by the engineers through the rock, the observation and ranging parties, and the pinpoint bombing flown by Caproni twin-engined bombers all decided the issue; by 1917 Italy was also filling the ranks with boys under eighteen, which carried the doctrine of grinding forward by attrition to its limit.
kits: 卡面這門一八六〇年的加特林機槍，是美國人理查德・喬登・加特林的六管人力轉動機槍：整挺機槍由人踩踏板或搖柄帶動，彈藥由卷盤供應，每分鐘可射六百至一千二百發，後坐力分散在六次擊發之間，這些原理正是連排機槍的原型。它在南北戰爭中被大量裝備英軍，一八七九年祖魯戰爭的伊桑德瓦納之役英軍也只配得上一挺；一八六〇年加里波第「千人團」進軍西西里時，美方援助的軍火中便有加特林機槍運抵，機槍第一次踏上義大利的土地。可是到一九一五年，加特林式在歐洲前線已被淘汰：義軍的連級機槍是菲亞特・雷維利 Mod.1914，六點五毫米口徑、水冷、頂置五十發彈匣、每分鐘二百五十至三百五十發，每營配三至六挺，多配給貝斯加利耶射手營與工兵，一九一六年改用百發彈鏈，一九一七年換上索洛圖恩後坐式機槍；奧軍以施瓦茨洛澤 M.07/12 為制式機槍，與曼利歇 M.95 步槍同為七點九二毫米。除槍械外，義軍有七十五與一百四十九毫米野戰砲、一百二十毫米迫擊砲及三十七毫米砲，奧軍則以十點五釐米榴彈砲、十五釐米榴彈砲與三十點五釐米臼砲壓制卡爾索的掩體，另有大量手榴彈、坑道炸藥，而窄軌輕便鐵路、騾車隊與卡車組成整條輸送網。
kitsEn: The Gatling gun of 1860 on this card is Richard Jordan Gatling's six-barreled, hand-cranked machine gun: the whole piece was driven by men on pedals or by a crank, the ammunition came off a drum, it could fire between six hundred and twelve hundred rounds a minute, and the recoil was spread over six separate discharges, which is the original principle of the section-level machine gun. It was equipped in large numbers by the Union in the American Civil War, and the British had a single Gatling at Isandlwana during the Zulu War of 1879; in 1860, when Garibaldi's Thousand crossed into Sicily, Gatling guns were landed with the American arms shipment, and the machine gun set foot on Italian soil for the first time. By 1915, however, the Gatling pattern had been swept off the European front line. The Italian section weapon was the Fiat Revelli Mod. 1914, 6.5 mm, water-cooled, with a fifty-round pan magazine on top and a rate of fire of two hundred and fifty to three hundred and fifty rounds a minute; three to six were allotted to each battalion, mostly to the Bersaglieri marksman battalions and the engineers; 1916 brought hundred-round belts, and in 1917 the Solothurn recoil-operated gun took over. Austria-Hungary used the Schwarzlose M.07/12 as its standard machine gun, chambered in 7.92 mm like the Mannlicher M.95 rifle. Beyond the small arms, Italy had 75 mm and 149 mm field guns, 120 mm mortars and 37 mm cannon, while Austria-Hungary used 10.5 cm and 15 cm howitzers and 30.5 cm heavy mortars to pound the Carso shelters, together with a great abundance of hand grenades and mine charges; light narrow-gauge railways, mule teams and lorries formed the whole transport network.
tactics: 義軍的戰術是教科書式的正面強攻：步兵以營縱隊在數百公尺至一公里距離上展開，在砲火準備不足的情況下向石砌堡壘推進，機槍與手榴彈在進攻前線展開，砲兵則以短時間反砲兵射擊壓制敵方觀察所。卡爾索台地是石灰岩喀斯特地形，地下坑道、洞穴與縱深堡壘構成層層防禦，義軍在一九一六年之後改以工程兵在岩層下挖掘隧道、裝填炸藥，再以迫擊砲與直瞄砲逐點清除，攻勢前的砲火準備由數小時延長到數日。義軍部分部隊實施夜間偷襲與小分隊滲透，一九一五年十月二十七日在戈里齊亞附近架設浮橋渡過伊松佐河，奪取西岸普拉瓦與塞拉一帶的橋頭堡，卻始終未能攻入戈里齊亞城區；一九一六年八月，第三集團軍以多日密集砲火終於突破塞拉入城，一九一七年十月的卡多里納戰役更以兩翼包抄與大量迫擊砲撕開奧軍縱深。奧軍的守勢則依靠堡壘的交叉射界、高射界臼砲與坑道反擊，把義軍的每一次正面進攻拖成逐點消耗。補給線的長度是這套戰術的硬約束：義軍後方樞紐在烏迪內方向，彈藥與糧食要靠火車、汽車再轉騾隊送上前線，這也是攻勢只能維持數日的根本原因。
tacticsEn: Italian tactics were the textbook frontal assault: infantry deployed in battalion columns across a few hundred metres to a kilometre, advancing on stone-built fortresses with insufficient artillery preparation, machine guns and hand grenades moving up with the assault waves, and the guns firing brief counter-battery missions to blind the enemy observation posts. The Carso is a limestone karst plateau, where underground galleries, caves and deep fortresses formed a layered defence; after 1916 Italy changed method, the engineers driving tunnels under the rock, packing them with charges, and then picking the positions off one by one with mortars and direct-fire guns, while the artillery preparation before each assault was stretched from a few hours to several days. Italian units also carried out night attacks and small-group infiltrations; on 27 October 1915 a pontoon bridge was thrown across the Isonzo near Gorizia, taking the western bridgehead around Plava and the Sella, though the town of Gorizia itself was never entered; in August 1916 the 3rd Army forced the Sella after several days of dense fire and took the town, and the Cadorina offensive of October 1917 tore open the Austrian rear with an envelopment on both flanks and a mass of mortars. The Austrian defence in turn relied on interlocking fortress fire, high-angle heavy mortars and counter-attack from the mine galleries, which turned every Italian frontal effort into a fight broken down point by point. The length of the supply line was the hard constraint on all of this: the Italian rear hub lay in the direction of Udine, and ammunition and food had to come by train and lorry before being transferred to mule teams for the last stretch, which is the root reason an offensive could only last a few days.
data: 可核對的數字大致如下，來源口徑不一，宜作概數看待。第一次伊松佐戰役自一九一五年六月二十三日打到七月七日，義軍傷亡約一萬四千，其中陣亡逾兩千，奧軍傷亡亦達數千。伊松佐戰線自亞得里亞海岸到阿爾卑斯山長約八十至一百公里，義軍在正面集結的兵力約二十餘個步兵師、三十萬人上下，野戰砲逾一千門，另有數百門迫擊砲；奧軍在戈里齊亞與多伯爾多台地部署大口徑砲與臼砲。到一九一五年底，義軍裝備的菲亞特・雷維利機槍數量以萬挺計，而第一次攻勢投入的砲火準備只有數小時。卡爾索一線的戰壕總長以數十公里計，最密集處雙方戰壕相隔不足百公尺，山腹隧道與地下道路構成另一套交通線。整個伊松佐戰役系列橫跨一九一五年六月至一九一七年十月，義軍傷亡以十萬計，奧軍傷亡亦達數萬。一九一七年十月德軍在斯梅倫附近實施突破，義軍在兩週內後退約一百公里，被俘與失散者近五十萬人，損失火砲上萬門。
dataEn: The figures that can be checked are roughly as follows, though the sources differ in what they count and they are best treated as approximations. The First Battle of the Isonzo ran from 23 June to 7 July 1915; Italian casualties were about fourteen thousand, of whom more than two thousand were killed, and the Austro-Hungarian losses also ran into the thousands. The Isonzo front stretched from the Adriatic coast to the Alps over some eighty to a hundred kilometres; the Italians massed on this front something like twenty-odd infantry divisions, around three hundred thousand men, with over a thousand field guns and several hundred mortars, while Austria-Hungary emplaced heavy cannon and mortars at Gorizia and on the Doberdo plateau. By the end of 1915 the number of Fiat Revellis in Italian service was measured in thousands, and the artillery preparation thrown into the first offensive was only a matter of hours. The trench system on the Carso ran to tens of kilometres, in the densest places the opposing trenches lay less than a hundred metres apart, and the galleries and underground roads in the mountain made a second traffic system of their own. The whole series of Isonzo battles stretched from June 1915 to October 1917; Italian casualties were counted in the hundreds of thousands and Austro-Hungarian losses in the tens of thousands. In October 1917 the Germans broke through near San Martino, the Italians fell back about a hundred kilometres in two weeks, close to five hundred thousand men were taken prisoner or went missing, and upwards of ten thousand guns were lost.
cause: 打起上來的原因，是義大利自認國家仍未完成。一八六六年威尼斯歸義大利，一八七〇年羅馬並入，但伊斯特拉半島、南蒂羅爾的蒂羅爾與特倫托仍屬奧匈，這是義大利民族主義者口中「未收復的領土」。一九一三年第二次塞拉耶沃刺殺危機之後，義奧關係急轉直下，義大利要求奧匈在這些地區讓步，並在一九一五年三月的倫敦密約中取得法國與英國對其參戰的承諾；奧匈在一九一四年七月對塞拉耶沃的最後通牒被拒之後，義大利擔心一旦奧匈在巴爾幹獲勝、國力坐大，日後更難收回這些土地，於是一九一五年五月二十三日對奧匈宣戰。開戰前的計劃是明確的：阿爾卑斯方向取守勢，把主力放在伊松佐與特倫托方向攻勢，卡多納希望用密集出擊速戰速決，因為義軍估計自己無力承受一場長期消耗戰，加拿大的源源運力與英國海上封鎖能否維持是另一個變數。宣戰後第一個月的準備，已顯示出砲兵不足、運輸吃緊與指揮系統對不稱這些致命弱點。
causeEn: The reason the war was fought is that Italy considered the nation still unfinished. Venice had come to Italy in 1866 and Rome in 1870, but Istria, the Tyrol and Trento in South Tyrol were still Austrian, and these were the unfinished territories of Italian nationalist rhetoric. After the second Sarajevo assassination crisis of 1913 relations between the two states deteriorated sharply: Italy demanded concessions in those areas and, in the secret Treaty of London of March 1915, obtained British and French promises in return for its entry into the war. When Austria-Hungary's ultimatum to Serbia was rejected in July 1914, Italy grew afraid that if Austria-Hungary won in the Balkans and grew stronger, these territories would be even harder to recover, and on 23 May 1915 it declared war. The plan drawn up before the war was explicit: a defensive posture in the Alps, with the main effort placed on the Isonzo and towards Trent, Cadorna hoping that repeated attacks would bring a quick decision, because Italy judged itself unable to bear a long war of attrition, while the uncertain supply of munitions and the durability of the British blockade were the other variables. The preparations of the first month after the declaration had already exposed the fatal weaknesses: too few heavy guns, transport in a bad state, and a command system out of proportion to the task.
impact: 後果是雙重的。義大利在卡爾索與伊松佐河兩岸付出的代價，換來了幾次真正成功的突破，也換來一支在一九一七年十月幾乎耗盡的陸軍：德軍突破之後，義大利北部大片土地淪陷，維吉尼亞與威尼托被占，戰俘與失散人數以十萬計，一九一七至一九一八年的糧食短缺與通貨膨脹把社會推到崩潰邊緣，軍隊內部的怨言與士兵委員會的出現，說明制度的斷裂早已發生。一九一八年十一月戰爭結束，義大利取得南蒂羅爾與的里雅斯特，但國內普遍認為所得不對等，詩人達農齊奧在一九一九年提出的「殘缺的勝利」成為整整一代人的心態。也正因這場戰役，義大利在戰後重整軍制：重砲兵與工程兵的份量提高，機槍與迫擊砲的編制標準化，航空工業亦在卡普羅尼、安薩爾多的設計局手中成形。卡爾索一線的坑道、洞穴與化石開挖，讓這片石灰岩地帶在戰後成為考古學與紀念性博物館的所在，卡普雷托的軍人陵園至今保存着一九一七年留下的旗幟。
impactEn: The consequences worked in two directions at once. What Italy paid on the Carso and along the banks of the Isonzo bought a few genuine breakthroughs, and it also bought an army that was spent by October 1917: after the German break-through large tracts of northern Italy fell, Venetia and parts of Veneto were occupied, prisoners and missing men ran to the tens of thousands, and the shortages and inflation of 1917 and 1918 pushed society to the edge of collapse, while grumbling in the ranks and the appearance of soldiers' committees showed that the fracture in the system had come long before. The war ended in November 1918 and Italy received South Tyrol and Trieste, but at home the settlement was widely judged to be too small, and the poet D'Annunzio's phrase in 1919, a mutilated victory, became the mood of a whole generation. Precisely because of this campaign Italy reorganised her army after the war: the share of heavy artillery and engineers was raised, the organisation of machine guns and mortars was standardised, and the aircraft industry took shape in the design offices of Caproni and Ansaldo. The galleries, caves and fossil digs of the Carso turned that limestone belt into a place of archaeological study and memorial museums after the fighting, and the military shrine at Caporetto still keeps the flags left behind in 1917.
result: 總結這一串戰役：義軍在一九一五至一九一六年先後五次大規模攻勢中屢攻不下，卡爾索的堡壘與多伯爾多台地幾乎沒有被突破，傷亡卻以萬計堆積；轉折點是一九一六年八月第三集團軍攻下戈里齊亞，以及一九一七年十月的卡多里納戰役實施戰術突破，義軍在卡爾索打穿奧軍防線，殲滅奧軍一個集團軍群的骨幹，戰果在紙面上相當可觀。可是戰略局面在幾週內被扭轉：十月二十四日德國在小戰區實施的突破，把整條伊松佐前線的縱深一次性打穿，義軍崩潰，一百公里的退卻與五十萬人的俘虜，把前面兩年的進攻成果一次抵銷。回到卡面這門一八六〇年的加特林機槍：它在一九一五年的前線早已不是作戰裝備，卻確立了連排機槍射擊、人力供彈、水冷散熱與六人射擊組這些要點，正是後來菲亞特・雷維利與施瓦茨洛澤在卡爾索上對付堡壘時倚重的骨幹。整場戰役的勝負，最後不決定於任何一件單兵器的射程，而決定於誰能先用連續火力與工程手段拆掉對方的堡壘。
resultEn: Summing up the series of battles: in the five large Italian offensives of 1915 and 1916 the attacks repeatedly failed, the fortresses of the Carso and the Doberdo plateau were barely breached, and yet the casualties piled up in the tens of thousands. The turning points were the fall of Gorizia to the 3rd Army in August 1916 and the tactical breakthrough of the Cadorina offensive in October 1917, when the Italians tore through the Austrian line on the Carso and destroyed the backbone of an Austrian army group, a result that looked considerable on paper. The strategic picture was reversed within weeks: on 24 October the German break-through in a minor sector punched the whole depth of the Isonzo front at once, the Italian army collapsed, and a hundred-kilometre retreat with half a million prisoners cancelled in one stroke the gains of the previous two years. Returning to the Gatling gun of 1860 on this card: by 1915 it was no longer a weapon in service on the front, yet it had established the points that counted, section-level machine-gun fire, ammunition fed by hand, water cooling and a crew of six, and those are exactly the points the Fiat Revelli and the Schwarzlose relied on when they went after the fortresses of the Carso. The issue of the whole campaign was settled not by the range of any single weapon but by who could take the enemy's fortifications apart first with sustained fire and engineering means.
